text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - U.S. exporters reported the sale of 101,600 tonnes of U.S. corn to Japan for 1996/97 delivery, U.S. Agriculture Department said. The marketing year opened last September 1.

RICE SALE - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs has bought 12,000 tonnes of white rice at $345 per tonne, a company spokesman said. The rice would be delivered in May.
SOYBEAN AND WHEAT TENDER - Taiwan is expected to tender for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans and for 68,000 tonnes of wheat over the next two weeks, Taiwanese traders said.

- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association would tender on Tuesday for two 34,000-tonne wheat shipments from the United States, traders said on Thursday. The two shipments are slated for delivery from PNW at April 25-May 15 and May 15-June 5.

BARLEY TENDER - Turkey's state grain board will seek bids for an international tender on April 29 to export 100,000 tonnes of feed barley and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley, a senior TMO official said on Monday.

WHEAT TENDERS - Iraq will tender on April 18 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat, several U.S. exporters said. The wheat will be slated for June arrival. Nearly 300,000 tonnes of wheat have arrived in Iraq under its Oil-for-Food deal with the United Nations, the Iraqi government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said on Sunday.

- CCC said it was seeking up to 7,220 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat, maximum moisture 13.5 percent, under the export program for Bosnia. The shipment period was set for May 7-31 and offers were due April 21.
WHEAT TENDERS - Syria offered 50,000 tonnes of hard durum amber wheat for June shipment. Bids were due April 15.
- USDA's Commodity Credit Corp said it will tender April 15 to buy 25,470 tonnes dark northern spring wheat for donation to Ghana. The wheat was due for May 1-25 shipment.
RICE TENDERS - Costa Rica will be tendering on April 30 for 26,500 tonnes optional origin long grain rough rice or 18,000 tonnes long grain milled rice.
- South Korea is expected to hold a tender at the end of June to buy 77,000 tonnes of rice to meet its 1997 quota under the World Trade Organization, U.S. Agriculture officials said.

MARKET TALK - The dry weather that has forced prices up across European grains markets is set to continue this week, forecasters said. On a nervous French market new crop moved clearly above prices for the old harvest for the first time this year on Monday, reflecting new warnings of potential drought damage, while LIFFE futures continued to soar.

... A cold snap that swept across the U.S. Plains last weekend damaged the nation's winter wheat crop, Al Peterlin, chief meteorologist of the U.S. Agriculture Department, said Monday. But the extent of the damage won't be known for several days until farmers inspect their fields, he added.

... Philippine wheat importers are expected to come back into the market this week on any price dips, Manila-based importers said on Monday. Ample supplies will keep the market for corn, rice, soybeans and soymeal quiet, the importers said. Traders said they have received inquiries from three millers for a total of 65,000 tonnes of wheat for May or June shipment.

... Political confrontation between Australia and Iran could depress world wheat prices if the standoff worsens, Australian wheat industry officials warned on Monday. If the Australian Wheat Board could not supply Iran with the two to three million tonnes of wheat it had contracted to sell in the 1996/97 year it would have to place the wheat on world markets, an AWB official told Reuters. "We would expect the price would be lower than we get from Iran," the official said.
... The United States on Monday promised an announcement within 24 hours on whether it would provide new food aid to famine-stricken North Korea. ((Doris Frankel 312-983-7305))
